data.name: Muqtada
data.gender_notes: Muqtada is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who is ordered, directed, or guided. Derived from the Arabic root q-t-d, which means to order or guide. In Islamic history, Muqtada Al Sadr is a prominent religious leader. The name Muqtada carries the meaning “Ordered, Directed, Guided” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muqtada usually hope their child will grow to embody ordered, directed, guided and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May Allah guide and direct you on the right path.
data.etymology: Muqtada belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ordered, Directed, Guided.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muqtada total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

His followers are known as the Sadrists, a vital political force in Iraq.

In Islam, the idea of being guided by Allah and following the right path is a fundamental belief. The name serves as a constant reminder for the person bearing it to strive towards seeking guidance from Allah and following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to live a virtuous and spiritual life. The name Muqtada is a call to be steadfast in faith, and to seek direction and guidance from Allah at all times.
